name: Knox County Schools
districtFact: KCS starts and ends the student year with half-days, schedules additional districtwide half-days during the year, and distinguishes systemwide in-service days, administrative days and student holidays. Its published 180 instructional-day total consists of 177 student instructional days plus three days accumulated through the daily seven-hour schedule.

about.title: The first student day is a half-day
about.content: KCS uses a staff preparation sequence before students report. Sixth- and ninth-grade orientation takes place during the final preparation day, then all students begin on a districtwide half-day. The final student day is also a half-day.

about.title: Half-days recur throughout the school year
about.content: The district calendar schedules several additional half-days for students, including dates near grading-period or semester boundaries. Families should use the assigned school's dismissal schedule for the exact release time.

about.title: The 180-day summary needs context
about.content: KCS prints 180 instructional days, then explains that the total is 177 student instructional days plus three days accumulated under the daily seven-hour schedule. The same summary separates administrative, scheduled in-service, unscheduled in-service and vacation days.

about.title: The calendar includes an eight-day cancellation allowance
about.content: KCS says up to eight instructional days may be canceled for inclement weather or serious outbreaks of illness before makeup days are required. Families should still follow current district alerts because the one-time ICS file does not update automatically.

calendarNotes: Use the official Knox County Schools calendar for districtwide attendance dates. The first and last student days are half-days, and several additional half-days occur during the year. Systemwide in-service and administrative labels describe staff duties; dates marked as student holidays are no-school days. School dismissal times, activities, athletics and building-specific changes should be confirmed with the assigned school. A downloaded ICS file is a one-time copy and does not update after a district revision or weather decision.

planningTips.title: Planning with the KCS calendar
content: Check the school's dismissal time for every districtwide half-day, especially the first and last student days.
Treat systemwide in-service dates marked as student holidays as full no-school days.
Keep the January staff day separate from Winter Break when identifying the actual student return date.
Use the official detailed calendar or school communication for activities, athletics and building events.
Watch KCS alerts when severe weather could change the published schedule.

districtFaqs.q: Are the first and last days half-days in Knox County Schools?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. The published KCS calendars identify both the first student day and the last student day as half-days. Families should check their school's dismissal schedule for the exact release time.

districtFaqs.q: Does 180 instructional days mean 180 full student days?
districtFaqs.a: Not exactly. KCS explains the total as 177 student instructional days plus three days accumulated under the daily seven-hour schedule. Several of the scheduled student days are districtwide half-days.

districtFaqs.q: Are KCS systemwide in-service days student holidays?
districtFaqs.a: Some are explicitly labeled as student holidays on the district calendar. The page preserves the official label for each date so families can distinguish student-free in-service days from staff preparation before the first student day.

districtFaqs.q: Why are sixth- and ninth-grade orientation listed before the first day?
districtFaqs.a: KCS schedules sixth- and ninth-grade orientation during the final staff preparation day. It is not the districtwide first day for all students; the full student calendar begins on the following published half-day.

districtFaqs.q: How many weather days can KCS cancel before makeup days are required?
districtFaqs.a: The published calendar says up to eight instructional days may be canceled because of inclement weather or serious outbreaks of illness before makeup days are required. Current district announcements control if the schedule changes.
